output.name: Tirsa — The Turning Gulls
output.myth: Mesket kept the watch on the north cliff, where the wind comes first. She did not look at the sea. She looked at the gulls. When they turned over the bay all at once, like a sheet shaken out, she called the boats in. Her eyes had gone grey from salt, and she said that was why she could see it. The Single Mitten never sets, and she said it watched the bay as hard as she did. One autumn the gulls turned and would not settle, so she called the boats, and the boats came in. Tavo came down the bay that night laughing. He tore three nets off the poles and took nothing that could be bargained back. Ennu's hawk hangs south over the drying racks, made to frighten gulls, and it never frightened hers. Mesket was not thanked, and she was not blamed. When she died they flew her up as a kite with a grey cloth tail. She still hangs over the Reach, facing the cold, turning when the gulls turn. Mend your net. Watch the bay.
output.finding: Find the Single Mitten, which never sets, then go a fist and a little more straight south of it to where the Turning Gulls hang above the bay.
